mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 3 months signals an accommodative monetary policy that compresses equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior 3 months, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS decline and positive returns is statistically insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.0% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that trigger risk-off sentiment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.0% in a month, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) over the prior 3 months indicates a broad-based economic slowdown that reduces corporate earnings expectations, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decline > 0.5% and INDPRO decline > 0.5% in prior 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST and INDPRO both decline by >0.5% in 3 months, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 3.0% and CPIAUCSL above 2.5% annually), the Federal Reserve's policy shift to combat inflation reduces equity risk appetite, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances during the specified trigger condition, or the correlation between the trigger condition and negative returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rising GDP growth rate (GDPC1) over the prior 3 months indicates expanding economic activity that boosts corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 growth has increased over the prior 3 months, or the correlation is insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) fall below 150,000 thousand persons, it signals a weakening labor market that increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS falls below 150,000, or the average return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in retail sales (RSAFS) and industrial production (INDPRO) over the prior 3 months indicates contraction in consumer spending and manufacturing output, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decline > 0.5% and INDPRO decline > 0.5% in prior 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS and INDPRO both decline by >0.5% in 3 months, or the interaction effect is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market downturn (HOUST falling below 1200 thousand units), the decline in residential construction activity reduces GDP growth expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST falls below 1200, or the average return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).
